clue.text: Destroy source of energy, resulting in awkward situation

parts.note: to scrap something is to destroy or discard it

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Wrecking a power supply leaves everyone in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an informal word for a predicament or tight spot one has got into.

clue.text: Officer and worker after a bit of work in the Kent area?

indicators.note: the insect comes after the region with its unit inside
the unit of work sits inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England, abbreviated SE

the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: An officer and a labourer turn up after a spot of work in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer in the army or a police officer of that rank.

clue.text: Gosh — having a drink before card game!

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink
my! is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise while pouring a drink before cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is a card game in which players collect sets and runs.

clue.text: Used badly, as a table that gets covered with things?

definitions.meaning: exploited or taken advantage of, the idiom for being imposed upon

definitions.text: as a table that gets covered with things?
definitions.meaning: literally, things are placed on top of a table, so it has things set on it

explanation.definitionFit: Being exploited is the idiomatic sense; literally a table has objects placed on it.

clue.text: Craft put around by the German merchant

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for craft is written back to front

parts.note: craft in the sense of skill or artistry is art
der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A merchant's ship is turned about by a German sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is someone who buys and sells goods, a synonym for merchant.

clue.text: Break in ceremony, allowing in thoughts from elsewhere

indicators.note: the word for ceremony lets the other piece into its middle

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
ESP, extrasensory perception, is receiving thoughts from another mind

explanation.surface: A ritual pauses to admit telepathic messages.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short pause or rest from something difficult.

clue.text: Put down achievement involving one in work

explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'in' makes POSIT first, and 'involving' then wraps the achievement around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposited means set down or laid in place, the same as put down.

clue.text: Oh, that we could soon have liquid deodorant!

definitions.text: Oh, that we could soon have
definitions.meaning: an exclamation of eagerness, as when longing for the holidays to arrive
a deodorant applied by a rolling ball in the bottle

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom welcomes something eagerly awaited; separately it names a liquid deodorant with a ball applicator.

clue.text: Doctor attending a mother twitching and full of excitement

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a tic is an involuntary twitching of a muscle

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a mother with a spasm in an exciting scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dramatic is thrilling and striking, full of excitement and suspense.

clue.text: Type of crop, formerly one thing of prime importance

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop
erst is an archaic word for formerly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer recalls one crop that used to matter most.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornerstone is literally a foundation block and figuratively the essential, most basic element.

clue.text: What's provided in a flexible manner

definitions.meaning: a stock of goods made available, as in a water or food provision
the adverb formed from supple, meaning bendily or pliantly

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means provisions furnished; as an adverb from supple it means pliantly, a rarer spelling of supplely.

clue.text: End of journey and we had returned a bit wet

indicators.note: sent back, so the contraction of we had is read from right to left

parts.note: we had contracts to we'd

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: At the close of a trip, travellers come home slightly damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy means moist with droplets of dew, so slightly damp.

clue.text: Approval for each to join religious campaign

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a mission is a campaign to spread a faith

explanation.surface: Each member needs approval before joining an evangelical drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission is consent or authorisation, a synonym for approval.

clue.text: An imperial unit intended to be heard in this report

indicators.note: the phrase is to be listened to rather than read, so its spoken sound gives the entry

parts.note: an ounce is an imperial unit of weight and meant means intended, giving the phrase an ounce meant

explanation.surface: A weights-and-measures notice is meant to be read out.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'an ounce meant' quickly and it runs into the answer; 'in this' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcement is a public statement or notice, the kind of report read out to people.

clue.text: Extended, as a picnic meal, say?

definitions.meaning: a picnic is a spread of food laid outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: It means opened wide; read as two words it describes a meal laid outdoors, like a picnic.

clue.text: Very poor little woman wanting man — and home primarily

indicators.note: put first, so the word for home leads the answer

parts.note: in means at home
Di is a short form of the name Diana
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A poor girl longs for a husband and a house above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' just sets the woman beside the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent is a formal word for needy or impoverished.

clue.text: Go up around edge of mountain with river all round — it's somehow divine

indicators.note: the river's name is wrapped all round everything built so far

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands

parts.note: to ascend is to go up

indicators.note: the edge here is the final letter of the word mountain

explanation.surface: A climber skirts a peak beside a river and finds the experience heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'around' makes ANSCEND first, then 'all round' puts the Midlands river outside it; the closing words just link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Transcendent describes what goes beyond the physical world, hence godlike or heavenly.

clue.text: Order given by a bishop, annoyance having no end

indicators.note: without its last letter, so the final letter of the word for annoyance is dropped

explanation.walkthrough: RR, Right Reverend, is the style of a Church of England bishop.

clue.text: Sort of globe you spotted in English dance

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone is seen at an English dance holding a globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted in' only links: you is seen next to English, then the dance follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye is a sphere, often called the globe of the eye.

clue.text: Surprisingly lionised — the province's departed veterans

indicators.note: arranged in a surprising way, so the letters are shuffled
gone away, so the letters of the province leave the mix

parts.note: Northern Ireland, often called the Province, is abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: Celebrated old soldiers from Northern Ireland have passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: In UK usage 'the Province' means Northern Ireland, NI; take N and I from LIONISED and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldies is an informal word for old people, those long in service like veterans.

clue.text: Our pals 'elp out, useful in every situation

explanation.surface: Cockney friends who will help out with anything are handy all round.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'elp suggests a London accent, but the word just supplies ELP.
explanation.definitionFit: All-purpose describes something with many uses, suitable for any job.

clue.text: Irish house cleaner finishing early

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day

clue.text: Tense as game finished without a winner

definitions.text: as game finished without a winner
definitions.meaning: a match ending level, a tie

clue.text: Farm animal, one that's disturbed bird

clue.text: Discharges that would be nasty for men at sea

clue.text: Son meeting snake is not so happy

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for son in family trees
the adder is Britain's only venomous snake

explanation.surface: A boy who runs into a viper is less cheerful afterwards.

clue.text: Alien in film follows map — to find this?

definitions.text: Alien in film follows map — to find this?

indicators.note: the film alien comes after the word for map

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
